The deduplication mechanism ensures that each item is unique across runs by intersecting with previous item sets. This creates a probabilistic space where new items are generated with zero overlap. The caption-media alignment primitive identifies a fundamental dualism: surface-level scroll notes versus deep semantic payloads. This discrepancy implies a need for dual inference paths—surface recognition for quick filtering and deep parsing for accurate categorization. Failure modes include misalignment due to poor captioning or incorrect media interpretation, leading to false positives in relevance scoring. The stochastic process is constrained by runtime and feed size, while deduplication maintains data integrity through persistent registries.
